subsystems.name: Regolith handling
subsystems.role: excavate, transport and size lunar soil.

subsystems.name: Consolidation energy source
subsystems.role: provide heat to fuse regolith or cure a binder.

subsystems.name: Deposition and forming
subsystems.role: place material in controlled layers or moulds.

subsystems.name: Structural design and reinforcement
subsystems.role: shape the built element to carry loads and contain pressure.

subsystems.name: Shielding and thermal control
subsystems.role: protect against radiation and temperature swings.

subsystems.name: Power and autonomy
subsystems.role: run robots and processes without humans on site.

buildSteps.title: Survey and site preparation
buildSteps.detail: Choose a flat, stable area near usable regolith; robots level the ground and remove large rocks.

buildSteps.title: Excavate regolith
buildSteps.detail: Robotic excavators dig loose soil and haul it to a processing area.

buildSteps.title: Process feedstock
buildSteps.detail: The soil is crushed, sieved to remove coarse fragments, and dried if needed.

buildSteps.title: Prepare construction method
buildSteps.detail: For sintering, no binder is added; for a concrete-like mix, a binder such as sulfur or a geopolymer is blended in.

buildSteps.title: Build foundation or landing pad
buildSteps.detail: A compacted or sintered base layer is laid down to spread loads and suppress dust.

buildSteps.title: Print or sinter the structure
buildSteps.detail: A robotic gantry or arm deposits regolith layer by layer; a laser, microwave or concentrated solar beam fuses each layer, or a binder sets it.

buildSteps.title: Cover and finish
buildSteps.detail: The shell is covered with loose regolith for radiation shielding, and airlocks, hatches and utilities are fitted.

buildSteps.title: Test and commission
buildSteps.detail: The structure is checked for leaks, thermal performance and structural integrity before use.

prerequisites.why: Earth-based simulants let engineers test sintering and binding before flight.
demonstrated in lunar analog environments, but not yet on the Moon.
laser and microwave fusing of regolith simulant works in the lab, but not at structural scale.
solar arrays have powered landers, but running heavy construction equipment through a lunar night is untested.
small robotic landers have reached the surface; delivering tonnes of construction equipment is not yet routine.
thick regolith overburden is a well-understood concept, though not yet built off Earth.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations sinter and 3D-print regolith simulant; robotic excavators run in lunar analog tests
pathway.unlocks: proof that local soil can be turned into solid shapes.

pathway.milestone: small robotic landers demonstrate excavation, sintering and a printed test patch on the Moon
pathway.unlocks: confidence in robotic construction in real lunar conditions.

pathway.milestone: robotic construction of a landing pad and a small shielded shelter, validated over a lunar day
pathway.unlocks: dust control and radiation protection for later missions.

pathway.milestone: large habitats and infrastructure built by robots, with humans assembling only specialised equipment
pathway.unlocks: a permanent lunar base that does not depend on Earth for bulk materials.
